Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath for approximately 1 hour, onset while sitting watching TV.
- Associated symptoms: New cough started yesterday; no sputum production reported; chest soreness with deep breaths (patient reports chest and C-section scar tenderness).
- Onset/duration/progression: Shortness of breath began over the last hour and came on suddenly; cough began the day prior.
- Recent events: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; postpartum, currently caring for newborn.
- Past medical history: No other medical problems reported.
- Previous surgeries: Cesarean section (4 weeks ago).
- Medications: Patient has been taking codeine for post-op pain fairly regularly; likely stopped taking it about 1 week ago. (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Social history: Lives with partner (partner at work at time of consult); baby present at home; patient alone at home currently.
- Allergies: Allergy to ibuprofen (reaction not specified).

Objective:
- Patient-performed pulse check: Patient counted 30 beats during instructed counting period; physician noted the heart rate is "slightly fast" at the time of the call.
- No other physical exam findings documented.
- No vital signs (blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature) or formal examination findings recorded.
- No investigations or imaging results available in transcript.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Shortness of breath:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Deep vein thrombosis leading to pulmonary embolism
     - Postoperative pain-related tachycardia/anxiety
     - Infectious respiratory process (e.g., bronchitis) — limited evidence
   - Investigations planned:
     - Immediate hospital evaluation to assess for thromboembolism (specific investigations not documented)
   - Treatment planned:
     - Advise urgent hospital attendance for assessment and management
     - If clot confirmed, anticoagulation to be given (specific agent/dose not documented)
     - Avoid taking codeine prior to hospital arrival (advised)
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Emergency department / hospital admission (patient to go to hospital by private transport; ambulance option offered)

2. Recent cesarean section / postpartum status:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Postpartum status following cesarean section
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Postoperative pain contributing to tachycardia and discomfort
     - Postpartum hypercoagulable state increasing risk for thromboembolism
   - Investigations planned:
     - Assessment during hospital visit to evaluate for postoperative complications and clot risk (specific investigations not documented)
   - Treatment planned:
     - Hospital evaluation; management to be determined by ED clinicians
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Emergency department / obstetric review as indicated by ED

3. Cough:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Acute cough (etiology undetermined)
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Viral or bacterial respiratory infection
     - Early pulmonary embolism (can be associated with cough/chest symptoms)
   - Investigations planned:
     - To be evaluated in hospital; no specific tests documented in transcript
   - Treatment planned:
     - Symptomatic/supportive care as determined by ED clinicians

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Objective vital signs (respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, temperature, exact heart rate), chest/respiratory and cardiovascular examination findings, details of codeine dose/route/frequency, specifics of ibuprofen allergy reaction, diagnostic test results (D-dimer, CTPA, lower limb ultrasound) and any imaging orders.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal interruptions; no significant inaudible sections.
